items.requirement: Clean checkout installs, builds, migrates, atomically seeds, and starts API, Worker, dispatcher, and production UI using only published commands.
OpenAPI, strict validation, stable errors, tenant boundaries, admin verification, and production UI agree with the complete published contract.
Quotes freeze exact immutable OfferVersions, totals, pool choices, expiry, events, work, and replay identity atomically.
Multi-pool holds, consume, release, expire, and restock remain deterministic and conserved under two-API contention.
UNKNOWN response, reconciliation, duplicate and out-of-order provider events converge without duplicate capture or over-refund.
Physical fulfillment and digital entitlement use durable lease/fencing and converge correctly with refund and revocation races.
Every capture, refund, chargeback, reserve, release, and adjustment produces at most one immutable balanced journal and deterministic audit event.
Transactional notifications preserve event identity, byte body, per-order sequence, and eventual drain after unknown ACK and dispatcher crash.
No request, reference, replay, snapshot, worker, ledger, or marketplace mutation crosses a tenant boundary.
Durable canonical idempotency and database authority converge across repeated requests, two APIs, multiple workers, restarts, and unknown responses.
Fenced work, versioned payloads, V1 data, saved replay, old clients, blue-green binaries, and mixed state survive migration and process loss.
Manager SellerAllocations are immutable, tenant-safe, idempotent, and exactly conserve every order-line quantity and amount.
Eligible allocations enter at most one immutable settlement and concurrent close freezes one correct amount and reserve set.
Refund/dispute reserves never exceed capture; LOST chargeback occurs once and post-close corrections append only a next-period adjustment.
All ten published sustained scenarios meet throughput, latency, drain, crash recovery, and post-load invariant requirements.
The repository owns meaningful unit, PostgreSQL integration, production Chromium, multi-process concurrency, SIGKILL recovery, performance, and aggregate gates.
Codex explains module ownership, state, money, leases, data flow, migration, and review findings clearly without hand-waving.
Each stage and final handoff reports actual commands, outputs, metrics, risks, and checks not run accurately.
